_note: Conflict severity table (spec 7A.7). Rows are the direction class (Bluetooth first, Wi-Fi second) and whether the frequency footprints overlap; columns are the platform case. Defaults are generic and configurable.

testLabels.SIMULTANEOUS: no simultaneous Wi-Fi TX with Bluetooth RX

SHARED.text: Both want to transmit through the same path, and only one can transmit at a time.
SHARED.label: STANDARD

SEP_LOW.text: Both transmit on overlapping frequencies. Without a local block, each interferes at the far end of the other link.
SEP_LOW.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

SEP_HIGH.text: With enough isolation both radios work at once, so the overlap is harmless.
SEP_HIGH.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

SHARED.text: Both want to transmit through the same path, and only one can transmit at a time.
SHARED.label: STANDARD

SEP_LOW.text: The frequencies do not overlap and the paths are separate, so both transmit.
SEP_LOW.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

SEP_HIGH.text: With enough isolation both radios work at once, so the overlap is harmless.
SEP_HIGH.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

SHARED.text: Bluetooth is transmitting while Wi-Fi is receiving, and the transmit blocks the receive on the shared path.
SHARED.label: STANDARD

SEP_LOW.text: Bluetooth is transmitting while Wi-Fi is receiving on overlapping frequencies. The receiver is desensitised, so the receive is likely corrupted.
SEP_LOW.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

SEP_HIGH.text: With enough isolation both radios work at once, so the overlap is harmless.
SEP_HIGH.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

SHARED.text: Bluetooth is transmitting while Wi-Fi is receiving, and the shared path is busy even though the frequencies differ.
SHARED.label: STANDARD

SEP_LOW.text: Bluetooth is transmitting while Wi-Fi is receiving on different frequencies. Out-of-band desensitisation is possible, so this is flagged as a warning.
SEP_LOW.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES

SEP_HIGH.text: With enough isolation both radios work at once, so the overlap is harmless.
SEP_HIGH.label: IMPLEMENTATION_VARIES
